before.imageAlt: Economics diagram: COST-01. Details are provided in the graph description.
before.graphDescription: Quantity is horizontal and dollars per unit vertical. Curves are MC, AC (average total cost), and AVC. At Q = 25, MC crosses AVC at its minimum of $30. At Q = 50, MC crosses AC at its minimum of $40, and AVC is $32. Between these quantities MC is above AVC and below AC.

before.imageAlt: Economics diagram: COST-02. Details are provided in the graph description.
before.graphDescription: Quantity is horizontal and dollars per unit vertical. At Q = 200, MC crosses AVC at its minimum of $10. At Q = 400, MC crosses AC (average total cost) at its minimum of $20; AVC there is $12. MC lies between the averages between their two crossings.

before.imageAlt: Economics diagram: COST-03. Details are provided in the graph description.
before.graphDescription: Quantity is horizontal and total cost vertical. The upper curve starts at $400, the middle curve starts at zero, and the lower horizontal line is $400. At Q = 120, point A on the upper curve is $1,200, point B on the middle curve is $800, and point C on the horizontal line is $400. These are total-cost observations; average costs such as ATC and AVC require division by quantity.
